executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC (Weeks 16-20, 2026) and PAHO (October 2025–May 2026) indicate multiple concurrent biological threats across human and animal health domains. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) in the Americas represents the most critical zoonotic threat given its BSL-3 select agent status and documented detections across the region through at least March 2026. Mpox (BSL-3), Yellow Fever, Dengue, and Measles are generating elevated alerts across the Americas, while Europe faces ongoing communicable disease pressures across five consecutive weekly reports. The simultaneous circulation of multiple respiratory pathogens including seasonal influenza, RSV, and pertussis adds significant burden to health systems in both hemispheres.
bottomLine: Multiple concurrent elevated biological threats—led by BSL-3 select agents H5N1 and Mpox in the Americas—demand immediate coordinated surveillance intensification and public health response across both hemispheres.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing spread
Zoonotic spillover risk with documented cases in the Americas requiring BSL-3 containment
Dual alerts from PAHO over consecutive months suggest sustained transmission pressure
threats.action: Activate zoonotic surveillance protocols; enforce BSL-3 handling requirements; expand human-animal interface monitoring; accelerate antiviral stockpiling and H5N1 vaccine preparedness

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating active circulation in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent with person-to-person transmission potential
Temporal proximity to global clade expansion events raises concern for new variant introduction
threats.action: Enhance case detection and contact tracing; ensure BSL-3 laboratory capacity; accelerate vaccination of high-risk populations; coordinate with ECDC on imported case surveillance

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 indicating renewed risk
Sylvatic transmission cycle activity in endemic zones
Vaccine-preventable disease with high case fatality rate if untreated
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in endemic and buffer zones; strengthen entomological surveillance; ensure adequate yellow fever vaccine supply and cold chain integrity

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 18 February 2026 amid historically high transmission season
Americas experienced record dengue burden in 2024-2025 with carryover risk
Aedes aegypti vector expansion linked to climate anomalies
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; activate dengue rapid response plans; monitor for severe dengue clusters; expand diagnostic capacity in high-burden countries

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026 indicating active transmission
Measles elimination status in the Americas region under threat
COVID-19 era immunization gaps creating susceptible cohorts
threats.action: Conduct vaccination coverage assessments; launch catch-up immunization campaigns targeting under-vaccinated populations; strengthen case-based surveillance and laboratory confirmation

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two consecutive PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained elevated activity
Multi-year global pertussis resurgence pattern extending into the Americas
Disproportionate risk to infants and immunocompromised individuals
threats.action: Review maternal and infant vaccination schedules; reinforce Tdap booster programs; enhance laboratory-confirmed case surveillance; communicate antibiotic prophylaxis guidelines to clinicians

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation

signals: PAHO alert 27 April 2026 marks start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
PAHO alert January 2026 flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation stressing health systems
ECDC weekly reports (Weeks 16-20, 2026) indicate ongoing European respiratory surveillance activity
threats.action: Promote influenza and RSV vaccination for high-risk groups; prepare ICU surge capacity; enhance sentinel surveillance at primary care level; coordinate with WHO on circulating strain monitoring

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 10 February 2026 indicating active risk
Vector-borne alphavirus with potential for large outbreak amplification in Aedes-dense urban environments
Co-circulation with dengue complicates clinical diagnosis and case management
threats.action: Strengthen arboviral integrated surveillance; train clinicians on differential diagnosis of dengue vs chikungunya; intensify Aedes aegypti vector control in affected municipalities

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents were flagged in this surveillance cycle. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) was the subject of two consecutive PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026), indicating sustained zoonotic activity in the Americas requiring BSL-3 laboratory containment and heightened human-animal interface monitoring. Mpox virus (MPXV), a BSL-3 select agent, was flagged in a PAHO update on 23 April 2026 documenting active circulation in the Americas. Both pathogens carry pandemic or public health emergency potential and require immediate escalation under national biosecurity and select agent program frameworks.
amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis treatment relies on macrolide antibiotics; any emerging macrolide resistance warrants urgent surveillance given the resurgent pertussis activity across the Americas
No explicit AMR-specific report detected in this cycle, but broad respiratory antibiotic use during simultaneous influenza/RSV/pertussis season elevates selection pressure for resistant organisms
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory burden (influenza, RSV, pertussis) is compressing diagnostic and healthcare system capacity across both hemispheres in early-mid 2026
Vector-borne disease co-circulation (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in the Americas suggests Aedes aegypti-driven syndemic risk amplified by ongoing climate-linked vector range expansion
Two consecutive PAHO H5N1 updates over four months indicate persistent zoonotic pressure rather than a single outbreak event, elevating pandemic preparedness urgency
Post-pandemic immunization recovery remains incomplete as evidenced by measles and pertussis resurgence alerts, pointing to systematic surveillance and vaccination system gaps
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert from PAHO (February 2026) signals an emerging non-infectious public health threat intersecting with pharmaceutical supply and patient safety systems
Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) and GLP-1 misuse alert (February 2026) together indicate a pattern of medication and substance safety events requiring toxicovigilance infrastructure
